# EvHint

> A hint is a small notification badge that signals unread or pending items — shown as a plain dot or a count, attached to an icon, tab, or menu item.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| ID | `evoq-ui:hint` |
| Layer | Atom (`src/atoms`) |
| Import | `import { EvHint } from 'evoq-ui'` |
| Template tag | `<EvHint>` or `<ev-hint>` |
| Source | `src/atoms/hint/EvHint.vue` |
| Extra attributes go to | the root `<span class="ev-hint">` |

## Design guidance

From the Figma page **Hint**, frame `3947:58190` (Hint). These rules are binding. Names in them are Figma's - the Vue API is the tables above.

### When to use

- Use to flag unread or pending items on an icon, tab, avatar, or menu entry.
- Use the dot type when only presence matters, not the exact count.
- Use a digit type to show a specific count of items.
- Use 99+ to cap large counts and keep the badge narrow.

### When not to use

- Don't use to label status or category  →  use Badge (`evoq-ui:badge`)
- Don't use as standalone text  →  use a Badge (`evoq-ui:badge`) or number
- Don't use as an interactive control  →  use Button (`evoq-ui:button`)
- Don't attach more than one hint to a single target.

### Do

- Anchor the hint to the top-right of its target
- Keep counts accurate and update them live
- Cap counts at 99+ to keep the width stable
- Announce changes to assistive tech (aria-live)

### Don't

- Show a 0 count — hide the hint instead
- Use a dot and a count at the same time
- Obscure the underlying icon or label
- Use it for long or multi-word text

## Contract

- Only the props, slots and events above exist on `EvHint`; anything not listed is not part of its API.
- An attribute that is not a prop (`class`, `id`, `aria-*`, `data-*`) goes to the root `<span class="ev-hint">`.
- Import it by name from `evoq-ui`; styles come once from `evoq-ui/style.css`.
- Refer to it by id `evoq-ui:hint` - the id stays the same if the component moves layer.
